title: Actor
description: A person, a role, a group, an organization, an external system or the system itself that takes part in processes (model/actors/). A role, group or organization may have members, which state it in their memberOf.

type.description: What the actor is. A role, a group and an organization may have members. system is the system itself (shown as Automatic): at most one per project (MQ9605).

memberOf.description: The roles, groups and organizations this actor is a member of. An actor in a process's list stands for itself and its members at any depth. Each entry names a role, group or organization other than the actor itself, once (MQ9601); memberships form no cycle (MQ9602).

relative.description: Makes this an actor worked out from the object a process runs for, per object at run time: the object's owner, the actor a field of the object names, or the members of a role, group or organization within a context object. Exactly one form (MQ9603). Such an actor is never a member and has no members, and a process that uses it must be able to work it out on every subject (MQ9604).

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

excludeStereotypes.description: Stereotype keys that a database schema's or a package's defaultStereotypes would give this element, left out with the stereotypes they imply. Only defaults can be excluded (MQ2029).

relative.title: Relative
relative.description: How an actor is worked out from the object. Give exactly one of owner, path, or membersOf (with within).

owner.description: The object's owner, held where each subject entry's owner names (or by the team's system when it names none).

path.description: The actor a field of the object names: to-one relation ends to follow, then a single-valued attribute or a to-one end. Ids must mean the same thing for every subject of a process that uses the actor (MQ9604).

membersOf.description: The members of this role, group or organization (not itself an actor from the object) within the context object that within reaches.

within.description: With membersOf only: the to-one relation ends that lead from the object to its context object; empty for the object itself.
